correctness.rationale: Exact derivation of the block transition matrix, stationary masses and complete eigenbasis gives the Kemeny expression and eigenvalue radius. Strict positivity of the derivatives away from balance proves the Kemeny optimum; monotonicity of the opposing radius branches proves the three-case spectral optimizer. Direct class-mass and within-class mode decomposition proves the exponential balanced mixing lower bound and 3-step star upper bound. Standalone `verify.py` uses rational elimination for hitting times, independent transition-power comparisons, and exact optimizer tests (12,354 comparison units). The claim is restricted to independent fresh snapshots with 0<p<1; finite checks are not treated as all-size proofs.

originality.rationale: The primary 2017 paper derives the single-neighbor transition reduction and cover-time bounds; its publicly accessible author manuscript was inspected in the relevant sections and end. It does not state the competing Kemeny/spectral-radius bipartition optima, crossover classification or the same-p exponential mixing contrast. Static nonbacktracking and static Braess analyses do not imply this temporal result without separate model-specific analysis. Queries across exact terms, aliases and parameter statements in published indices and mathematical finding records yielded no implication-equivalent finding; priority remains qualified, not certified.

value.rationale: The theorem exhibits a structural conflict between average stationary-target hitting and worst-case relaxation on the same temporal network family, with graph-size-uniform optimum classifications and an exponential-versus-three-step mixing separation at the same fixed availability. The precise spectral crossover tells when network degree balancing ceases to be relaxation-optimal; this information is not just a known-table value, an arbitrary numerical slice, or a small improvement.
